title: Invoice timestamp hysteresis and rate-limit credit hedging
creator: Asha Raman
description: Problem: Sporadic invoice inaccuracies observed when late rate-limit credit adjustments arrive near hourly boundaries. Root cause analysis found two coupled issues: (1) invoice-line anchoring uses the last-seen usage timestamp which can flip when a late delta arrives within a tight buffer window, and (2) the rate-limit credits system emits multiple small adjustment events that are currently folded into exports without hysteresis, causing proration and rounding to oscillate between Stripe line items and NetSuite allocations. Impact: customers see transient negative/duplicate line items and previewed invoice totals that differ from final charged amounts. This affects accounting reconciliation and triggers support tickets for enterprise customers with Reserved Capacity.
proposed_solution: Introduce a timestamp hysteresis layer in the export pipeline: hold exportable hourly buckets open for a configurable 'hedge_window' (default 8 minutes) to absorb late pulses. Aggregate rate-limit credit deltas inside that hedge_window into a single reconciliation delta and apply deterministic cent-rounding at the bucket boundary. Implement idempotent export signatures (seqnum + hedge_window marker) so retries or concurrent reconciler runs produce stable Stripe line items. Add a fallback policy that, past the hedge_window, emits an 'adjustment' line with a standardized metadata tag so NetSuite/finance can easily map corrections. This preserves invoice stability while keeping backfill latency bounded.
tradeoffs_and_considerations:
- Increasing hedge_window reduces noisy invoices but delays earliest finalization of line items; default 8 minutes chosen from observed late-pulse distribution (90th percentile ~5m).
- Single-aggregate approach loses granularity on micro credit events for internal auditing; mitigated by retaining raw delta logs and providing an export-forensics view in Console.
- Need to ensure any buffering doesn't break SLA for 'real-time' usage-based billing customers; we will make hedge_window adjustable per-tenant and expose a metric for 'finalization_lag'.
- Interaction with Stripe invoice preview: we must keep preview stability; we'll update preview logic to use the same hedge_window heuristics.
acceptance_criteria: No duplicate negative line items in production exports for a 7-day rolling window after rollout
Export signatures include hedge_window marker and are idempotent across reconciler retries
NetSuite import mappings unchanged; finance sign-off on adjustment-line tagging
E2E test harness simulates late pulses and asserts deterministic Stripe preview vs final invoice within cent rounding rules
Metric: percentage of invoices that change by > $1 between preview and final decreases by 95% for affected customers
implementation_steps: Add hedging logic to export worker: buffer incoming usage deltas by hour + hedge_window
Modify export proto to include hedge_window_seq and deterministic cent-round algorithm
Implement export signature writer and idempotent reapply path in reconciler
Add adjustable tenant config and migration to set conservative hedge_window for enterprise customers
Update preview path used by Console to apply same hedging behavior
Create NetSuite import sample showing adjustment-line mapping and metadata tag
Ship CI tests and E2E simulation harness that replays delayed pulses from last 30 days of production traces
Deploy to canary region and monitor metrics for 48h before full rollout
testing_plan: Unit tests for buffer collapse and cent-rounding logic
Property tests that simulate concurrent reconciler runs and assert idempotency
E2E scenario: replay 10k delayed pulses; assert final invoice equals golden ledger within 1 cent per invoice
Shadow exports to 'billing-shadow' Stripe account for 7 days and compare with current exporter outputs
Manual finance validation: run NetSuite import on sample adjustments and confirm allocations
metrics_and_dashboards: console-dashboard: Billing > Export Reconciler > Hedge Window Impact
rollout_plan: Stage 2: 5% tenant rollout for 48h with hypervigilant alerting
Stage 3: 100% non-enterprise tenants, then staged enterprise config flips after finance confirmation
Rollback: revert feature flag and run one-off reconciler to normalize any open buckets
